title: Ehud and King Eglon
reflectionText: Israel had served Moab eighteen years before they cried out, and the deliverer Yahweh raised up was an unlikely one — a left-handed man who could hide a sword where no one thought to look. The account does not linger to admire the killing; it moves quickly to a freed people and a land at rest. Eighteen years of bondage, and then eighty of rest. What has kept its grip on you far longer than it should have?
editorialNotes: PAL Daily supervised production 2026-07-26, Batch F. Judges 3:12-30 ONLY. Adult lane (Ehud's assassination of Eglon) — kidFriendly false. The killing is told plainly and briefly, keeping the difficult detail (the fat closing over the blade, 3:22) without added gore and without glorifying it; the account's own quick move to deliverance and rest is preserved.
